reviews.title: Disappointing update.
reviews.text: I’m normally not one to write reviews on apps (this is actually the first one on my apple account), but TunnelBear used to be great! Very heavy emphasis on USED TO. I just haven’t used it recently and the latest changes have left me (and others, based on the recent reviews) upset. I used to use TunnelBear as a good VPN to read and watch shows, specifically for the free feature of accessing VPNs that made it look like I was from other countries. It’s disappointing that one of the best features of the app is now locked behind a paywall. While I have tried to use “Fastest” as a VPN anyway, it can barely function and takes a while to load almost every website, despite being called “Fastest.” I also randomly disconnect from the VPN at times, which then means the website refreshes and any “progress” trying to load the website in the first place is reset. It is annoying to see the direction this VPN is going and I will probably be deleting this app and finding a better VPN soon. I suggest anyone considering this app and reading the reviews to look elsewhere if they want to use an actually functioning VPN.

reviews.title: Was good, NERFED by a paywall in 2026
reviews.text:
Recently, Tunnel Bear began to paywall basic features. Features like being able to connect to countries other than the one you presently live in. Most user of VPN services will note that that is one of the main features of a VPN, connectivity to other countries’ internet. Thats now paywalled, on top of limited data for free users (which I never had a problem with)

And it’s a shame too. This app was incredibly intuitive and easy to use. But if you live in a large country, it’s now worthless because you can only connect to a select number of nearby hubs. So if you’re in Europe, maybe you can connect to a neighboring country, but in the US your options are a different US location, or sometimes Canada. 

So this app is now pointless.

reviews.title: Rugpull of features turns most generous VPN into least
reviews.text:
They’ve arbitrarily cut off the ability to choose which country you connect to with the free VPN plan. I dislike that they used to offer it, and no longer do.

Before this, consumers of TunnelBear would subscribe to the paid plan after a short time of feeling grateful for being able to ‘try out’ the VPN with minimal restrictions under the free plan. I was one of those consumers. That generous business model made it seem as though the company was genuinely interested in offering its service to consumers, and not insecure about squeezing every last drop; consumers could go at their pace and choose to sign up for a paid plan in order to support the company choosing to operate in this manner. That company no longer is. TunnelBear no longer wants to present itself in that light. It is no longer a service provider, it is a profit generator.

I’m not going to support a company that uses false good will to get me on board and, then, once it’s a large enough, stable enough share of the market, pivot to a more greedy model and place new consumers in a worse position.

This feels like a slap in the face, considering how many people I have recommended TunnelBear to over the past years.

Rather than maintaining a paid subscription, I will be uninstalling entirely, or just sharing accounts with another with a paid plan, in either way resulting in less money for the company.
